task_2.title: Restore assertion diff output in importlib import mode
task_2.description: Pytest 8.3.3 restores assertion rewriting behavior for modules imported with `--import-mode=importlib` when spec discovery depends on the module file path, so failing rewritten asserts once again show useful comparison details instead of only a bare assertion failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that failing rewritten `assert` statements continue to display assertion comparison details when pytest is run with `--import-mode=importlib`, including package-based test modules whose import spec cannot be resolved from the package location alone.

expectation.grounded: When pytest imports a test module with `--import-mode=importlib`, assertion rewriting must still apply even if initial spec lookup from the provided import path returns no module spec. Pytest should successfully resolve the module from the concrete module location when needed so that a failing rewritten `assert` raises an `AssertionError` with the usual introspected comparison output and diff details, rather than only a bare `AssertionError`.
expectation.conceptual: Running pytest in importlib import mode should not strip away rich assertion explanations. If a test imported from a package fails a rewritten `assert`, users should still see the same helpful comparison and diff output they expect from normal pytest assertion introspection.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve existing import behavior when a module spec is already found, must not alter the public failure type for rewritten assertions, and must not regress assertion rewriting support for modules loaded through `--import-mode=importlib`.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to restoring missing assertion detail output without changing how successful imports or ordinary assertion failures behave in other scenarios.

behavior: Under `--import-mode=importlib`, pytest now continues module spec resolution using the concrete module path when spec lookup from the initial import path does not find a spec.
Modules resolved through that path remain eligible for pytest assertion rewriting instead of bypassing rewritten assert handling.
When a rewritten `assert` fails in such a module, pytest once again shows enriched assertion output with compared values and diff-style explanation rather than only a bare `AssertionError`.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is run with `--import-mode=importlib` against a test module inside a package and the module cannot be resolved from the package location alone, the module should still be imported successfully for assertion rewriting.
When a rewritten string or value comparison `assert` fails in that imported module, pytest should display the usual assertion explanation with comparison details and diff output.
When the module spec is already resolvable without fallback, pytest should preserve existing import and assertion-reporting behavior.

task_1.title: Prevent descriptor side effects during fixture discovery
task_1.description: Pytest 8.3.3 fixes a collection-time regression where fixture discovery could execute @property and similar instance descriptors on collected objects. Upgrading removes those unintended side effects during discovery while preserving normal detection of real pytest fixtures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.3.3 prevents collection and fixture discovery from executing @property or other instance descriptors on collected test objects, especially in unittest-style suites, while still discovering declared fixtures normally.

expectation.grounded: During fixture discovery, pytest should inspect attributes without invoking instance descriptors such as property, cached-property-like descriptors, or other __get__-based instance descriptors unless the attribute has already been identified as a @pytest.fixture. Fixture-marked attributes must still be discovered, including fixtures with explicit fixture names, and then resolved from the instance in the normal way.
expectation.conceptual: Collection should remain side-effect free for non-fixture computed attributes. Unrelated descriptors must not run just because pytest is discovering fixtures, while real fixtures continue to be available with their expected names and behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress normal fixture discovery for legitimate pytest fixtures. The change must avoid accidental descriptor access on inspected object instances without changing fixture availability, fixture naming, or ordinary discovery behavior for classes and modules.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only remove unintended descriptor execution during discovery. It must not change which real fixtures are exposed or how users reference them.

behavior: Pytest no longer evaluates non-fixture @property attributes merely because collection or fixture discovery inspects a test object.
Custom instance descriptors that execute code from __get__ are not invoked solely by fixture discovery when they are not fixtures.
Descriptors that would otherwise raise exceptions, exit the process, or perform expensive work on access no longer cause those effects during discovery alone.
Attributes explicitly declared as pytest fixtures continue to be discovered and exposed under their default or explicitly assigned fixture name.
acceptance_criteria: Given a unittest-style test class with a non-fixture @property that raises an exception or performs expensive work, when pytest collects the suite, it should not execute that property during collection.
Given a collected object with a custom non-fixture descriptor that raises from __get__, when pytest performs fixture discovery, it should not trigger that descriptor.
When an attribute on a collected object is marked with @pytest.fixture, pytest should still discover it and make it available under its declared fixture name.
Collection should not fail, exit unexpectedly, or become slower solely because unrelated instance descriptors exist on collected objects.

task_3.title: Restore BaseException typing for ExceptionInfo.errisinstance
task_3.description: Pytest 8.3.3 fixes a typing regression in ExceptionInfo.errisinstance by restoring support for BaseException subclasses, so static analysis once again accepts valid uses such as checking SystemExit while leaving runtime behavior unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 8.3.3 restores backward-compatible typing for ExceptionInfo.errisinstance so code that checks BaseException subclasses, including non-Exception cases such as SystemExit, remains supported.

expectation.grounded: The ExceptionInfo.errisinstance API should accept either a single exception class or a tuple of exception classes typed against BaseException rather than only Exception. Calls made on ExceptionInfo[BaseException] should remain type-correct for mypy and continue to support checks against subclasses such as SystemExit.
expectation.conceptual: Calling errisinstance on captured exceptions should remain a valid supported operation for any Python exception class, including exceptions outside the Exception hierarchy, and the upgrade should remove static type-checking failures introduced by the narrower annotation.

constraints.grounded: Do not narrow ExceptionInfo.errisinstance to Exception subclasses only. Existing uses that pass BaseException subclasses, whether singly or in tuples, must remain accepted by the API contract, and existing Exception subclass checks must continue to work without changed runtime semantics.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must restore backward-compatible typing without changing how the method behaves for current callers.

behavior: ExceptionInfo.errisinstance is typed to accept BaseException subclasses as its argument, whether provided as one class or as a tuple of classes.
Static type checking should accept calls on ExceptionInfo[BaseException] that check SystemExit or other BaseException subclasses outside the Exception hierarchy.
Existing errisinstance usage with ordinary Exception subclasses remains supported with no user-visible runtime behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: When code captures BaseException and later calls exc_info.errisinstance with SystemExit, that usage should be supported after upgrading to 8.3.3.
When errisinstance is called with a tuple of BaseException subclasses, that form should remain part of the supported API contract.

When projects run static type checking on code that uses ExceptionInfo.errisinstance with BaseException subclasses, the upgrade should no longer fail because of the narrowed Exception-only typing introduced in the prior release.

task_4.title: Restore pytest typing compatibility on Python 3.9 and lower
task_4.description: Pytest 8.3.3 fixes a typing-only compatibility issue for Python 3.9 and earlier so projects that type-check pytest plugins or custom collection nodes retain correct subclass return types instead of degraded inference.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to pytest 8.3.3 preserves correct static typing behavior on Python 3.9 and lower for users authoring pytest plugins or custom node types, especially when class methods typed as returning the concrete subclass are used in extension code.

expectation.grounded: On Python versions <= 3.9, pytest's type information should remain compatible with static type checkers by using a `Self` definition that works on those interpreters. Publicly consumed APIs and patterns that rely on subclass-preserving return types, such as `Node.from_parent(...)` on custom `Item` or collector subclasses, should continue to infer the concrete subclass rather than collapsing to `Any` or an imprecise type in typed plugin code.
expectation.conceptual: Projects using pytest with static type checking on older Python versions should get the same concrete type inference they would expect on newer Python versions. Creating custom pytest nodes through standard pytest APIs should remain type-safe without requiring version-specific workarounds.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade is limited to typing compatibility and must not change pytest runtime behavior, collection behavior, or public execution semantics. Existing subclass-returning API contracts should remain intact across supported Python versions, with the only intended change being correct type-checker interpretation on Python <= 3.9.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve developer typing experience only. It must not alter how pytest runs, collects, or instantiates objects at runtime.

behavior: Pytest 8.3.3 provides Python <= 3.9-compatible `Self` typing for affected typed APIs.
Static analysis of typed pytest extensions on Python 3.9 and lower should preserve concrete subclass return types for subclass factories such as `from_parent(...)`.

Typed plugin code that returns instances created through these APIs should no longer require Python-version-specific casts or disabled diagnostics solely because pytest's type metadata used `typing.Self` on unsupported interpreter versions.
The change affects typing compatibility only and does not introduce runtime behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria: When a project type-checks pytest plugin or custom node code against pytest 8.3.3 on Python 3.9 or lower, subclass-producing pytest APIs should infer the concrete subclass type rather than an unspecified fallback type.

When extension code returns an object created through the standard pytest subclass factory pattern, the declared return type should remain compatible with static analysis on Python 3.9 and lower without extra compatibility-only casts.
Upgrading from 8.3.2 to 8.3.3 should not change observable pytest runtime behavior; the improvement should be limited to typing compatibility.

task_6.title: Respect verbosity when rendering assertion messages
task_6.description: Pytest 8.3.3 fixes assertion reporting so the optional message in `assert condition, msg` follows the active verbosity level when rendered, especially for long non-string message objects that were previously shortened too aggressively.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that failed assertions written as `assert condition, msg` respect the active verbosity level when showing the assertion message, so long messages are not always truncated the same way regardless of verbosity.

expectation.grounded: When pytest renders a failed assertion of the form `assert condition, msg`, the `msg` portion should use the framework's existing verbosity-sensitive safe representation rules. If `msg` is not a string, its displayed `AssertionError` representation should expand or abbreviate according to the current verbosity level instead of always using the same shortened form.
expectation.conceptual: Assertion failure messages should become more informative as verbosity increases. Long object-based assertion messages should be abbreviated at normal verbosity when needed, but shown with more detail at higher verbosity so users can inspect the actual difference or content.

constraints.grounded: This change should only affect formatting of the assertion message payload. String messages must continue to preserve their existing escaping and newline behavior, and non-string messages must still be rendered through safe representation logic rather than bypassing output size protections.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve how much of the assertion message is visible without changing whether the assertion fails, the overall failure structure, or the safety of generated output.

behavior: Pytest now applies verbosity-aware shortening rules when formatting non-string messages passed as the second argument to `assert condition, msg`.
Long non-string assertion messages may still appear abbreviated at default verbosity levels.
At higher verbosity levels, the same non-string assertion messages should be rendered with more detail or without abbreviation, consistent with pytest's general assertion display behavior.
Existing handling for string assertion messages remains unchanged apart from the surrounding failure report.
acceptance_criteria: When a test fails with `assert condition, msg` and `msg` is a long non-string object, pytest should include the message in the `AssertionError` output using verbosity-dependent truncation.
When the same failing assertion is run at a higher verbosity level, pytest should show more of the non-string message representation than it shows at default verbosity.
When the assertion message is already a string, pytest should preserve its established formatting behavior while continuing to report the assertion failure normally.
When verbosity is not increased, pytest should continue to abbreviate overly long non-string assertion messages as needed instead of emitting unsafe or excessively large output.

task_5.title: Preserve parametrization IDs in reported nodeids on Windows
task_5.description: Pytest 8.3.3 fixes Windows nodeid rewriting so that making a test path relative to the invocation directory no longer alters parametrization IDs. Verbose and summary reporting now preserve user-visible parameter text consistently when tests are run from a subdirectory.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest reports parametrized test identifiers without corrupting parameter values when tests are run from a subdirectory on Windows.

expectation.grounded: When pytest converts a nodeid to be relative to the invocation directory, it should rewrite only the filesystem path segment before the first `::`. The test name and any parametrization ID content after `::` should remain unchanged in the reported nodeid, including forward slashes, backslashes, drive-style prefixes, repeated slashes, and literal `::` text contained in parameter representations.
expectation.conceptual: Running tests from a nested working directory should not change how parametrized case IDs are displayed. Pytest should preserve the parameter text the user supplied while still showing the test file location relative to where pytest was invoked.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not normalize or reinterpret non-path segments of a nodeid as filesystem paths. Behavior should remain unchanged when no cwd-relative rewrite is needed, and distinct parametrization IDs must remain distinct in reported output.
constraints.conceptual: Only the location portion of a reported test identifier may be adjusted for the current working directory. The descriptive portion of the identifier must stay stable and unambiguous across environments.

behavior: When pytest is invoked from a directory different from the project root, it should make only the test file path portion of a reported nodeid relative to the invocation directory.
Parametrization IDs shown after the test function portion of the reported nodeid should preserve forward slashes on Windows instead of converting them into path separators.
Parametrization IDs containing Windows-like paths, standalone slashes or backslashes, repeated slashes, or embedded `::` text should remain visible as distinct reported identifiers.
acceptance_criteria: When a parametrized test has an ID containing `/` and pytest is run from a subdirectory on Windows, the reported identifier should preserve `/` in verbose output and failure summaries.
When distinct parametrization IDs such as `/` and `//` are reported from a subdirectory on Windows, pytest should display them as distinct cases rather than collapsing them through path conversion.

When a parametrization ID contains text such as `C:/path`, `\\`, `C:\\path`, or `a::b/`, pytest should preserve that text after the test function portion of the reported identifier while still making the test file path relative to the invocation directory.

task_8.title: Clarify deselection reporting for custom collection filters
task_8.description: Pytest 8.3.3 clarifies the contract for plugins and local hooks that filter collected items in pytest_collection_modifyitems: when items are removed, they are expected to notify pytest through pytest_deselected so deselection reporting and downstream plugin notifications remain consistent.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that custom collection filtering performed during item modification explicitly reports deselected tests so pytest's deselection accounting and plugin notifications remain consistent.

expectation.grounded: When a pytest_collection_modifyitems implementation removes collected Item objects from the items list, it should also call the pytest_deselected hook with the deselected items. This applies to hook implementations that filter out tests, not to hooks that only reorder or otherwise retain the full item set. Plugins that implement pytest_deselected should continue to receive these notifications, and the hook may be invoked more than once across a run.
expectation.conceptual: If custom collection logic excludes tests after collection, the run should treat those tests as explicitly deselected rather than silently dropped. Users and plugins should observe consistent deselection notifications and reporting whenever collection-time filters remove tests.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for pytest_collection_modifyitems implementations that only reorder items or leave the collected set unchanged. Preserve the existing pytest_deselected integration model in which plugins may implement the hook to observe deselections, and allow multiple deselection notifications within a single session.
constraints.conceptual: Only actual deselection should trigger deselection reporting. Non-filtering collection customizations must continue to behave as before, and integrations that listen for deselection events must keep working across repeated notifications.

behavior: Custom filtering in pytest_collection_modifyitems is expected to emit a pytest_deselected notification for every group of items removed from the collected item list.

The pytest_deselected hook serves both as an extension point for observing deselected tests and as the required notification mechanism when plugins or local hooks deselect items during collection modification.
When deselected items are reported through pytest_deselected, other plugins can react consistently and pytest's selected versus deselected accounting remains coherent from a user perspective.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin or local hook removes tests inside pytest_collection_modifyitems, the removed tests should be reported as deselected through pytest_deselected.
When collection-time filtering deselects tests, users should observe coherent deselection-aware run reporting rather than those tests disappearing without deselection accounting.
When another plugin implements pytest_deselected, it should be notified about tests removed by custom pytest_collection_modifyitems filtering.
When pytest_collection_modifyitems only reorders items or leaves the collected set intact, no deselection notification should be required.

task_7.title: Handle missing verbosity when terminal plugin is disabled
task_7.description: Pytest now tolerates runs where the terminal plugin is disabled and the standard verbose option is not registered. Verbosity-dependent reporting and logging paths fall back to default non-verbose behavior instead of failing at runtime.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that disabling the terminal plugin does not cause pytest to crash because verbosity configuration is missing, and ensure that failure reporting, logging, and other verbosity-sensitive output paths continue to work with default verbosity behavior.

expectation.grounded: When pytest is invoked without the terminal plugin, behavior that relies on verbosity should use `Config.get_verbosity()` and treat an unavailable `verbose` option as global verbosity `0` instead of raising `ValueError`. Assertion-related failure rendering, live CLI logging adjustments, import error formatting, fixture display, node exception formatting, duration reporting, and collection-finish status output should continue to run and apply their existing verbosity thresholds.
expectation.conceptual: Disabling terminal output should not break test execution or failure reporting. If verbosity is unavailable, pytest should behave as if it is running at the default verbosity level, while preserving the usual extra-detail behavior when verbosity is explicitly enabled.

constraints.grounded: Do not require plugins or user hooks to manually populate `config.option.verbose` to avoid crashes. Preserve current threshold-based behavior for verbosity levels greater than the default, including logic that controls traceback filtering, exception detail truncation, fixture detail output, summary visibility, and CLI logging output cleanup.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be backward-compatible: existing quiet/default/verbose behavior should remain consistent, and only the missing-verbosity case should change by safely falling back instead of failing.

behavior: Pytest must no longer raise a missing-option error solely because the terminal plugin was disabled and the `verbose` option was not registered.
Global verbosity lookups must fall back to `0` when verbosity is unavailable, so output paths default to non-verbose behavior.
Verbosity-controlled formatting for import errors and exception representations must continue to apply the same detail thresholds, using the fallback verbosity when needed.

Verbosity-sensitive reporting for fixture display, duration summaries, and collection-finish status messages must remain available without depending on terminal-plugin registration of the verbose option.
When live CLI logging is enabled, pytest must still normalize low-verbosity output behavior without crashing if verbosity state is missing.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is run with the terminal plugin disabled and a test fails with an assertion error, it should complete the run as a normal test failure instead of crashing with a missing verbosity-option error.
When verbosity has not been registered, any feature that decides output detail from global verbosity should behave as though verbosity is `0`.

When verbosity is explicitly increased, pytest should continue to expose the same higher-detail reporting behavior as before for traceback rendering, exception detail display, fixture output, and related summaries.
When live CLI logging is active under default or missing verbosity, pytest should continue to adjust output cleanly and remain operational.

task_9.title: Clarify tmp_path_retention_policy configuration syntax
task_9.description: Version 8.3.3 corrects the documented example for configuring tmp_path_retention_policy so it matches the actual accepted syntax. The update prevents users from copying a quoted value that is treated as invalid configuration.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that documentation and upgrade guidance for configuring `tmp_path_retention_policy` show the valid syntax and do not suggest quoted values that fail when used in configuration.

expectation.grounded: The `tmp_path_retention_policy` option should be documented with bare values such as `all`, `failed`, and `none`. Observable behavior remains that quoted values such as `"all"` are invalid input and can raise a `ValueError` during configuration parsing.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be shown the correct way to configure `tmp_path_retention_policy`: use the supported policy names directly, without quotes. Documentation should match the real accepted format and avoid examples that lead to configuration errors.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the supported policy set or their meaning. `tmp_path_retention_policy` continues to accept only `all`, `failed`, and `none`, and this update should not alter tmp path retention semantics or introduce new parsing behavior.
constraints.conceptual: This update should correct guidance, not change feature behavior. Existing valid configurations should continue to work exactly as before.

behavior: Documentation and release guidance present `tmp_path_retention_policy` values in the accepted unquoted form.
The supported policy names remain `all`, `failed`, and `none`.
Quoted policy values remain invalid configuration input and may surface as a configuration-time `ValueError`.
acceptance_criteria: When users consult the configuration example for `tmp_path_retention_policy`, it should show an unquoted policy value such as `all`.
When a user configures `tmp_path_retention_policy` with one of the supported bare values, the configuration should be understood as valid.
When a user copies a documented example, the example should not imply that quoted values are supported.
The documented meanings of `all`, `failed`, and `none` should remain unchanged.

task_10.title: Pytest 8.3.3 typo-only patch release
task_10.description: The 8.3.3 update is a maintenance-only patch release that corrects typos in internal comments and documentation-related text, with no intended change to pytest's public runtime behavior or API semantics.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from pytest 8.3.2 to 8.3.3 is treated as a non-functional patch update that preserves existing runtime behavior, because the release only corrects wording and typo issues.

expectation.grounded: Pytest 8.3.3 should keep the observable behavior of existing APIs and flows unchanged, including configuration access such as `Config.getini`, fixture scope ordering behavior, legacy hook mark handling, and debugging/PDB entry behavior. The release note and code diff indicate typo and wording corrections only, with no public API additions, removals, or runtime signal changes.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to 8.3.3 should not change how pytest runs, reports, orders fixtures, reads configuration, or enters debugging flows. Users should experience the release as a maintenance cleanup rather than a feature or behavior change.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce changes to return values, warning behavior, exception behavior, item ordering, tracing/debugging behavior, or public API shape as part of this patch-level upgrade. The release must remain compatible with behavior expected from 8.3.2.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must be safe and behaviorally neutral for existing users. It should not require application code changes or alter observable pytest outcomes.

behavior: The release corrects typo and wording issues only.
No new user-facing features, options, or public APIs are introduced.
No observable runtime behavior changes are expected in configuration lookup, fixture ordering, legacy hook processing, or debugging entry flows.
Existing usage compatible with pytest 8.3.2 should remain compatible with pytest 8.3.3 without behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria: When a project upgrades from pytest 8.3.2 to 8.3.3, it should not need to change its pytest configuration or usage patterns.
When users invoke existing pytest features, they should observe the same runtime behavior and outcomes as in 8.3.2.

When interacting with configuration access, fixture ordering, hook handling, or debugging flows, the upgrade should preserve prior behavior with no new warnings, exceptions, or semantic differences attributable to 8.3.3.
The release should be understandable to users as a maintenance-only patch with no functional regression risk introduced by new behavior.
